Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

themselves pronoun

also by themselves, they themselves

classical

Varr. RR 3.16.38: restituunt sē ac revīvēscunt
Liv. 21.31.1: ad iter sē parāre jubet

suī, sibi, sē (sēsē)

pronoun, reflexive: genitive suī, dative sibi, accusative and ablative sē; the same for every gender and number

themselves (as object), referring to the subject

The same sē as in the singular: restituunt sē, they recover (themselves). Not to be confused with “each other”, inter sē (see each other).

Other words

  • ipsī, ipsae, ipsa — themselves (for emphasis: they themselves, of their own accord)

    pronoun, intensive (plural of ipse), declension · classical · Plin. NH 18.107: ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs; Cic. Div. 1.74: valvae clausae sē ipsae aperuērunt (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse, Div. 1.37.74)

    Stresses the people or things: ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs, the citizens made their bread themselves. With the reflexive it agrees with the doer or with the object: valvae clausae sē ipsae aperuērunt, the shut doors opened of themselves.

Examples

  • quae enim sīc concaluērunt, restituunt sē ac revīvēscunt

    For those that have been warmed in this way recover and come back to life.Varr. RR 3.16.38

  • mōrēs quoque sē inter lūdendum simplicius dētegunt

    Character, too, shows itself more openly in play.Quint. 1.3.12

  • corpora cūrāre atque ad iter sē parāre jubet

    He tells them to see to their bodies and get themselves ready for the march.Liv. 21.31.1

  • valvae clausae sē ipsae aperuērunt

    the shut doors opened of themselvesCic. Div. 1.37.74 (Lewis & Short)

  • pistōrēs Rōmae nōn fuēre ad Persicum ūsque bellum … ipsī pānem faciēbant Quirītēs, mulierumque id opus maximē erat

    There were no bakers at Rome until the war with Perseus … the citizens made their bread themselves, and it was chiefly the women’s work.Plin. NH 18.107

  • jam hortum ipsī agricolae succīdiam alteram appellant

    And the garden the farmers themselves call their second flitch of bacon.Cic. Sen. 56

See also they, himself, itself, each other.
